title: The Border Boys Are Back: Sunny Deol and Akshaye Khanna Reunite After 28 Years — and This Time, the War Is in a Courtroom
excerpt: Ikka drops on Netflix July 10. It's their first film together since the 1997 classic that made an entire generation weep for the Indian soldier — and the pairing alone makes it unmissable.
body:
Some reunions you wait for so long that when they finally happen, you almost don't believe them. **Sunny Deol** and **Akshaye Khanna** haven't shared a frame since they broke India's collective heart in **J.P. Dutta's Border** twenty-eight years ago. That film — with its dust, its tears, and its Anu Malik score that still makes grown men cry at weddings — turned them into an iconic screen pairing. Then they went their separate ways. Deol did Gadar, then Gadar 2. Khanna disappeared into meaty villain turns and emerged as 2026's most in-demand antagonist.

<youtube></youtube>

Now they're back together. And the battlefield has changed.

## The Setup

**Ikka** is a legal thriller directed by **Siddharth P. Malhotra** — the man who gave us the quietly devastating *Maharaj* on Netflix last year — and it drops on the platform on **July 10, 2026**. The premise is exquisitely uncomfortable: Sunny Deol plays a celebrated, incorruptible lawyer who is forced to defend a murder accused he himself once prosecuted. That accused? **Akshaye Khanna**.

So the two men who once stood shoulder to shoulder at Longewala are now on opposite sides of a courtroom. One bound by law, the other bound by whatever it is that makes Akshaye Khanna's eyes go still and dangerous. The casting is so good it almost feels like cheating.

> "As a storyteller, I'm always looking for stories that challenge me emotionally and creatively, and Ikka has been one such journey. Having Sunny Deol step into the role of a lawyer, a character space audiences have so loved him in, alongside such phenomenal performers, felt like everything coming together at the right time." — **Siddharth P. Malhotra**

## The Cast Around Them

The supporting cast is quietly stacked. **Dia Mirza** and **Tillotama Shome** — two actors who couldn't be more different in their approach — anchor the film alongside the leads. **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, **Akansha Ranjan Kapoor**, and **Shishir Sharma** round out the ensemble. The script comes from **Althea Kaushal** and **Mayank Tewari**, and the background score is by **Julius Packiam**, who has a knack for making courtroom silences feel like ticking bombs.

Malhotra has spoken about wanting to make a courtroom drama that's as much about personal relationships and moral compromise as it is about the pursuit of justice. That tracks. *Maharaj*, his last Netflix outing, took what could have been a standard period piece and turned it into something far more uncomfortable and human. If he brings the same instinct to Ikka, this could be special.

## Why It Matters for the Diaspora

Let's be real: for NRIs of a certain generation, **Border** isn't just a film. It's a rite of passage. It's what your dad put on every Republic Day. It's "Sandese Aate Hai" playing in the background of every long drive home from the gurudwara. The idea of seeing Deol and Khanna together again — older, greyer, carrying the weight of three decades of very different careers — is the kind of thing that hits differently when you're watching it from Houston or Leicester or Brampton.

And it's on Netflix, which means there's zero friction. No hunting for showtimes, no checking which theatre near you is playing the Hindi version. It's just there. July 10. Press play.

## The Bigger Picture

Ikka also lands at an interesting moment for both actors. **Sunny Deol** is having a genuine late-career renaissance — *Gadar 2* proved the old magic is intact, and he has *Batwara 1947* lined up for August 14. **Akshaye Khanna**, meanwhile, has become Bollywood's most compelling screen villain. After the monstrous Sher-e-Baloch in *Dhurandhar 2* — a performance so controlled it barely let you breathe — he's riding a wave of critical love he hasn't seen since *Dil Chahta Hai*. He also has *Drishyam 3* in the pipeline, where he'll presumably continue making Ajay Devgn sweat.

Putting them in a courtroom — with Deol as the righteous lawyer forced to bend and Khanna as the accused who may or may not deserve mercy — is the kind of high-wire character work that straight-to-streaming films were invented for. No box-office pressure. No songs shoehorned in. Just two actors who know exactly what they're doing, locked in a room.

## The Verdict

Watch it for the reunion. Stay for what Malhotra does with it. And keep tissues nearby — not because it's *Border*, but because watching Sunny Deol and Akshaye Khanna share a frame again after 28 years is going to make you feel things you weren't prepared for.

**Ikka** premieres exclusively on Netflix on **July 10, 2026.** Mark your calendar.
